o: Explain why programs need translation into machine code.
Choose a language for a scenario and justify it.
c: High-level code is designed to be readable: for example, score = score + 1. It is usually easier to develop, debug and maintain than processor-specific instructions.
Machine code is made of binary instructions executed by a CPU. Assembly is a low-level form using short instruction mnemonics: you only need to recognise the difference, not learn an assembler.
Processors execute machine code. Source programs written in high-level languages need translation into executable instructions before or while running.
A school application benefits from readable, maintainable, portable code. Direct processor control may justify a lower-level approach, but is harder to maintain and is processor-dependent.

m.title: Model two linked benefits
m.q: A school is developing a timetable application. Explain TWO benefits of using a high-level language. [4 marks]
st: The application will be maintained and may be used on different computers. Choose benefits relevant to that context.
High-level code is more readable [1], so staff can understand and change the program more quickly [1].
High-level code is generally more portable [1], so moving to a different processor is likely to require less rewriting [1].
Award a knowledge mark and a linked consequence for EACH explained benefit. Do not simply name two features.

w: A controller needs precise access to processor instructions. Explain ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of using a low-level language. [4 marks]
Instructions can give precise processor control [1] useful for managing the device hardware [1]. They are processor-specific [1], so code may need rewriting for different hardware [1].
Compare high-level with low-level code in terms of readability and portability. [4 marks]
High-level programs are usually easier for people to read [1] and are more portable [1]. Low-level code corresponds closely to CPU instructions [1] and is usually processor-specific [1].
A school wants an attendance application that teachers can edit and run on different computers. Recommend a language level and explain TWO reasons. [4 marks]
High-level [1]; the code is easier to read and maintain as rules change [1]; it is usually more portable [1], making it easier to move across processor families [1].

wSteps: What matters to a device controller?
Identify how the code interacts with processor instructions.
Think about portability to different CPUs.
Control [1] with hardware explanation [1]; processor-specific [1] with a consequence [1].
Make two columns: readability and portability.
Explain who finds high-level code easier to use.
Relate low-level code to the CPU instruction set.
High-level readable [1] and portable [1]; low-level processor-close [1] and CPU-specific [1].
Identify the suitable level, not a brand name.
Give two benefits tied to this school scenario.
High-level [1]; maintainability linked [1]; portability [1] and use on new hardware [1].

k.q: What value will be printed after the second assignment?
p: Check the final value of score before print.
Change the first assignment to 7. Predict the new output.
Extend by adding score = score * 2 before print.
k.a: Original output 6; changed first assignment gives 9; extending the original with multiplication prints 12.

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
High-level code is more readable [1] and generally more portable [1]. Low-level code resembles processor instructions [1] and normally depends on the processor instruction set [1].

A microcontroller needs precise hardware control. Explain an advantage and a disadvantage of using assembly. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
Assembly is close to machine instructions [1], allowing detailed processor control [1]. It is processor-specific [1], so a change of hardware could require rewriting [1].

A medical practice is creating an appointment-booking program that will need regular updates. Explain TWO advantages of using a high-level language. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.

Readable code makes maintenance and correction easier [1], saving development time when appointment rules change [1]. High-level code is generally portable [1], reducing rewriting if the system is moved to other processor types [1].
v: A programming language with readable instructions less tied to a particular CPU.
A language close to machine instructions, such as assembly language or machine code.
Binary instructions the CPU can execute.
How easily a program can be moved to different hardware or systems.
Software that converts source code into a form the computer can execute.
x: Machine code is made of processor instructions that the CPU executes.
r: For Q=(A AND B) OR C, find Q when A=1, B=0 and C=0. [2 marks]
A AND B = 0 [1], so Q = 0 OR 0 = 0 [1].
State the output of a NOT gate for an input of 0. [1 mark]
In the array [7,2,9,4], state the zero-based index of 9. [1 mark]
Explain why a truth table with three independent Boolean inputs requires eight rows. [2 marks]
Each input can be 0 or 1 [1], giving 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 combinations [1].
